before: Changes in fungal-associated volatiles may provide a screening window before visible spoilage. AeroSense aims to connect insect OR/Orco receptors in HEK293 cells, a weak-fluorescence reader and a fly-inspired decoder. Current evidence includes endpoint reporter images from one batch, a separate P2 kinetic pilot, reader simulations, fluorescein calibration observations and computation on external metal-oxide sensor data. The intended output is a prompt for follow-up testing, not a mycotoxin concentration or a food-safety clearance.
after: Fungal deterioration causes substantial crop losses, highlighting the need for accessible tools for early, on-site detection. Our project, AeroSense, is a modular biohybrid olfactory platform designed for agricultural screening, with banana production as its intended first application. The platform brings together a cell-based sensing array expressing Drosophila odorant receptors and their coreceptor ORCO in HEK293 cells, GCaMP6f fluorescence reporting, a compact four-channel optical reader, and a fly-inspired neural network for odor-pattern decoding. We documented reporter expression and conducted exploratory measurements of fluorescence kinetics. We also built and tested the optical reader using fluorescent standards, with transport and optical modeling informing its design. In parallel, computational studies evaluated odor-pattern decoding on external sensor datasets. Discussions with agricultural researchers and potential users shaped the proposed screening workflow and a shared-access deployment strategy. Together with reusable analysis code, hardware documentation, and educational resources, this work lays the groundwork for an accessible screening tool to guide follow-up inspection and confirmatory testing.

A separately prepared blank is needed to assess specificity.
